newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end lower on strong yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end lower on strong yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures settled lower on Wednesday, pressured by the yen's strength against the dollar and weaker soybean futures in Japan, traders said.
Prices were 20 to 110 yen lower, with the benchmark July 1998 down 40 yen at 13,850 yen per tonne.
Activity was lacklustre with estimated volume at 26,886 lots.

Prices started mostly in line with the firmer Chicago market overnight, but fell into negative territory on the stronger yen. "Corn prices are likely to drift sideways until the USDA report due out on June 30," one trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.60 per bushel at 0814 GMT, down from $2.60-1/4 at Tuesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.29 a bushel at 0815 GMT, against $8.31 at Tuesday's close.
